newsitem.title: UK: UK RETAIL SALES GROWTH EASED IN JULY-CBI SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: UK RETAIL SALES GROWTH EASED IN JULY-CBI SURVEY.

text.p: Annual growth in British retail sales eased slightly in July and is expected to continue at a broadly similar rate in August, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday.

Its July distributive trades survey showed 56 percent of retailers reported increased sales volumes in the period (July 3 to July 30) compared with the same period a year ago while 21 percent said they were down.
This leaves a positive balance of 35 percent reporting increased volumes compared with 39 percent in June. The CBI said 37 percent of retailers had expected an increase.
Looking ahead, the survey showed 32 percent of retailers expect volumes to increase in August.
The three monthly average indicates the underlying sales growth is continuing at a strong rate although it remains below the annual growth reported between July 1996 and January this year.
With the exception of off-licences and footwear and leather retailers, all sectors reported an increase in sales in July compared with a year earlier.

Sectors reporting the highest volume growth included clothing, chemists, and those goods related to the housing sector such as furniture and carpets, durable household goods, china and do-it-yourself products.
Sudhir Junankar, associate director of economic analysis at the CBI, said underlying sales growth continued to be relatively stable in July.
"Retail sectors closest to the housing market have been among the best growth performers, no doubt helped by consumers starting to spend their windfalls."
He said sales growth in August was expected to be steady rather than spectacular. "(This suggests) upward momentum in consumer demand remains firmly under control."
The slight slowdown in the growth of wholesalers' volumes in the year to July was less than the marked deceleration that had been expected.

The survey continues to show a mixed picture within wholesaling with office equipment, durable goods and electrical installation material reporting a pick up in sales while agricultural machinery, clothing, textiles and the footwear sector reported a further decline.

Motor traders' sales volumes fell in July in line with expectations. Growth is expected to pick up markedly in August, with sales expectations the highest since March 1994. Sales were above average for the time of year and orders placed with suppliers were broadly unchanged.
